title: Regular oriented link diagrams
statement: Let $\pi\colon\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^2$ be the orthogonal projection forgetting the last coordinate, and let $L$ be an oriented link contained in $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$. The projection $\pi\circ L$ is **regular** when (1) it is an immersion (the projected derivative never vanishes); (2) its only multiple points are finitely many double points, and the two branches at every double point meet transversely (their projected tangent lines are distinct); (3) there are no triple or higher multiple points. A **regular oriented link diagram** $D$ consists of the image $\pi(L)$ together with (a) the over/under datum at every double point (which branch lies above, read from the forgotten coordinate) and (b) the orientations of the strands induced by $L$. Diagrams are decorated immersed oriented $4$-valent planar graphs; a diagram is understood up to planar isotopy (next item).
strategy: The definition fixes the ambient plane, the projection and the over/under convention; the finiteness and transversality clauses are exactly Conditions 1-3 of the source and are what make the slicing arguments of the Reidemeister items finite.
